presentation.label: Multitrack stems to the card
presentation.summary: Hold UP and press REC to open STEMS, then record each track, MAIN, CUE and the inputs to their own WAV files while the sequencer plays.
presentation.overview: Stem Rec writes a take to the card while the sequencer plays: every track after its fader, the main mix, the cue mix and the four inputs, each as its own 44,100 Hz WAV file in 16 or 24 bits, for up to 60 minutes. Each take gets a folder in AUDIO/!STEMS. It uses no effect slot. Card builds only.
highlights: UP then REC opens and closes STEMS; REC alone stays stock.
T1 to T8, MAIN, CUE and the input pairs AB and CD, each on or off; a pair records as one stereo file or two mono ones.
16 or 24 bits; each track's file is its share of MAIN, so levels, scenes and the crossfader are in it.
The take starts with the sequencer and stops with it, on YES, after 60 minutes, or when the card falls behind.
usage: Include Stem Rec in a card build. Hold UP first, then press REC: STEMS opens.
Choose the sources with UP, DOWN and YES: T1 alone is on at boot, at 24 bits.
Press YES on STEM REC: it arms, and the take starts when the sequencer plays (at once if it already does). Stop the sequencer to end it.
Wait until STEM REC reads DONE before you pull the card or power off. The files are in AUDIO/!STEMS/<take>/.

controls.name: STEM REC
controls.doc: The take's state: READY, ARMED, the time, SAVING, DONE or NO CARD, or a failed take's error. YES arms a take, cancels an armed one or stops a running one.

controls.name: T1
controls.doc: Records track 1 after its fader. With MASTER TRACK on, T8 reads MASTER and is left out.

controls.name: T8
controls.doc: Records track 8 after its fader; reads MASTER, and is left out, while MASTER TRACK is on.

controls.name: MAIN
controls.doc: Records the main mix as it is mixed.

controls.name: CUE
controls.doc: Records the cue mix as it is mixed.

controls.name: AB
controls.doc: Records inputs A and B as they arrive. LEFT and RIGHT pick the row's checkbox. With STEREO off the row reads A and B, each with its own checkbox, and each input that is on records as a mono file.

controls.name: AB STEREO
controls.doc: On: inputs A and B record as one stereo file. Off: as one mono file each.

controls.name: CD
controls.doc: Records inputs C and D, as AB does.

controls.name: CD STEREO
controls.doc: On: inputs C and D record as one stereo file. Off: as one mono file each.

controls.name: 24 BIT
controls.doc: On: 24-bit files. Off: 16-bit files, half the card's writing.

limitations: Card builds only: over USB a module lives in the base's 768 KiB ColdFire pool, and Stem Rec needs an 8 MiB ring and runs a writer task of its own for each take.

No YES double tap on the main page in this version: in octabam a second YES within 0.5 s arms a take, but APPLY SCENE patches that stock site and a card build has no key bus. UP + REC and the YES on STEM REC's own row work as upstream.
Nothing is saved: at every boot T1 alone is on, at 24 bits, both pairs stereo. Stem Rec writes nothing into projects.
A power cut or a card pull before DONE leaves the take's files at 0 bytes: each file's length is set only at the end.
The card must keep up: a 24-bit stereo file needs 264,600 bytes a second. When the card falls behind the ring fills and the take stops with RING FULL; its files still play.
With MASTER TRACK on, T1 to T7 and CUE are 32 samples (0.73 ms) early against MAIN, and the track files do not sum to MAIN.
Sample memory: a card build with Stem Rec gives up the 10,487,808-byte DRAM platform reserve from Flex sample RAM, shared with any other DRAM module; its 8 MiB ring sits inside it.

resources.recorded: 5 November 2026; STEMMW1 on an MKII, emulator counts and the link map

storage.label: ColdFire code, data, rings and stack
storage.display: 8,436,254 B of its own, inside the 10.49 MB DRAM platform reserve
storage.conditions: The 8 MiB ring, the writer's 8 KiB stack, 7 KiB of sector copies with 480 bytes of padding, the 23,210-byte unit, the 8,568-byte loader appendix and 28 bytes of hook sites; any DRAM module also creates the 10,487,808-byte platform reserve taken from Flex sample RAM, which holds them. See TESTING.md.

processing.label: ColdFire, per audio block
processing.display: 13,992 of 95,782 cycles a block at 11 files (measured); about 15,505 with every source
processing.conditions: The frame hook's longest frame on the unit, 53 us at eleven 24-bit files, at 264 MHz; every source at 24 bits scaled from it by the emulator's instruction counts (4,468 / 4,032). The writer task runs outside the audio interrupt. See TESTING.md.

impact.conditions: One take with every source on at 24 bits. Estimates describe source structure, not measured hardware headroom.

cpu.rationale: The frame hook runs every audio block, a few hundred instructions while idle and a few thousand while every source records; the writer task waits on the card.

dsp.rationale: No DSP program, effect slot or DSP state is added: the hook reads the audio read-back blocks the stock code already has.

memory.rationale: An 8 MiB ring in DRAM, inside the platform reserve every DRAM module shares.

tests.summary: On Yves's MKII (5 November 2026, image STEMMW1): two takes of eleven 24-bit files, both OK, every file whole, the frame hook 53 us at most (13,992 of 95,782 cycles a block). Under the emulator the card builds alone and beside APPLY SCENE, TUNER and USB AUDIO OUT, boots, and fills its gain table from the OS (verify.py).
gates: verify.py: the card build boots under ot_emu, its DRAM runtime reads back equal to the link, its gain table holds the OS's 774 bytes, its regions lie in the reserve, and it builds beside APPLY SCENE, TUNER and USB AUDIO OUT
Hardware report for this source and image (STEMMW1, 6618b451...): yvesrosius, MKII, 2026-11-05 (reported; TESTING.md)

conditions.parameterExtremes: 16 and 24 bits, every source on or off, the input pairs stereo or mono, MASTER TRACK on and off: the emulator counts the hook at 396 instructions a frame idle, 937 with T1 alone, 4,032 with the eleven files measured on the unit and 4,468 with every source at 24 bits, the most (the source's cost gate, 400 frames each). The unit measured eleven files at 24 bits: 53 us at most.
conditions.parameterModulation: Levels, MAIN LEVEL, scenes, the crossfader, LFOs and p-locks reach Stem Rec only through each track's gain: a track whose gain moves on a frame takes the ramp path, about 100 instructions more on that frame, otherwise the flat path. The unit's takes ran the project with its own levels. No MIDI CC or other control path.
conditions.modeSwitching: Arm, start on the first frame the sequencer plays (the files' layout is latched once, on that frame, inside the frames measured), stop on the sequencer, on YES, after 60 minutes or on RING FULL. The take's end and the card writes run in the writer task, outside the audio interrupt.
conditions.maxLoad: One instance. Every source at 24 bits (fourteen files) is the most: estimated from the unit's 53 us at eleven files scaled by the emulator's 4,468 / 4,032 instructions, 58.7 us, 15,505 cycles of the 95,782-cycle block at 264 MHz. The unit's takes ran with the project's Static tracks streaming from the card; the hook and the stock frame routine together took 104 us at most.
conditions.inputConditions: The hook's instructions depend on the source mask and the fader moves, not on the audio, except the limiter: a track whose gain can exceed unity takes the limited loop, one compare a sample on the common path; the source's unit tests drive every loop form with rail samples. Measured with the project's audio; no silence or full-scale take on the unit.

regions.name: The DRAM unit: code, state, gain queue and gain table (.text; no BSS)
The platform loader and packed unit appended to the image
The four rewritten hook sites in stock code
The rest of the platform reserve, given up from Flex sample RAM

memory.conditions: Exact layout of the card build (STEMMW1's MAIN OS): the unit at 0x40a955e0..0x40a9b08a with no BSS, the three DramRegions from layout.json, the 10,487,808-byte platform reserve 0x40a955e0..0x41495de0 that any DRAM module creates and shares, its unused 2,060,150 bytes counted here; the boot stage (8,336 bytes at 0x40a9c000) is temporary inside that unused part. No heap. The writer stack's peak, 1,560 of 8,192 bytes, is from emulator runs of the source; no canary was measured on hardware.

hardware.summary: Yves flashed OCTATRACK_STEMMW1.bin (454,608 B, SHA-256 6618b451...) on his MKII on 5 November 2026 and recorded two takes of eleven files at 24 bits (T1 to T7, MAIN, CUE, AB, CD), 11.8 s and 3.1 s, both ended by the sequencer: both status OK, every WAV whole with its .ot and the take's STATS.TXT, the ring at most 32% full, the frame hook 28 and 29 us on average and 53 us at most. STEMS opened with UP + REC, YES armed, and a double YES on the main page did stock's ARM ALL only.
limitations: Two short takes; the fourteen-file maximum configuration, a take of T1 alone and a reboot were not run on the unit.
The track files were not checked against MAIN: the project leaves T8 out of every take, as with MASTER TRACK on, when MAIN is T8's output (inferred).
MKII only; not run on an MKI.
